content.comment_body: I have two 3-wire PT100 sensors connected to an [product_name] module to control water temperature in a chiller. Last year, the [product_name] display showed correct temperatures. Now, after reconnecting the main circuit breaker and powering on the [product_name], the only temperature value shown is -50. I've checked all connections between the module and the base unit, verified onboard analog inputs, and tested the sensors—everything appears fine. I'm puzzled by the consistent -50 reading. Does this indicate that the [product_name] module board might need repair?
Please upload your program in a ZIP file.
My program contains around 400 blocks, and I'm confident it's not the source of the issue since it worked for a full year. Are you suggesting the program might be the cause?

Some standard questions: - What is the status of the Run/Stop LED on the [product_name] module? - What values are displayed for the analog indicators on the [product_name]? - With sensors disconnected, can you measure any voltage between U+ and U- at the sensor terminal? What is the measured value? - Does the disconnected sensor have any connection to ground? - Is the sensor's IC connected to U+ in any way? Regards [user_name] (translated with Google)

Hello, It turned out both the module and one of the PT100 sensors were faulty. I resolved the problem by replacing them. Thank you for your assistance. However, I'm still unclear about why the module and sensor failed, especially as the environment isn’t damp. I'm worried this might happen again next year.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced an issue with a [product_name] module consistently showing -50 for temperature readings, although the system had been working properly the previous year. After extensive troubleshooting, the user resolved it by replacing both the affected module and a sensor but remains confused about the underlying cause and concerned about possible future failures.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the temperature measurement system to operate reliably each year without unexpected hardware breakdowns. They are seeking to understand why the fault occurred to help prevent similar issues going forward.
